questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Local culture and ease of access to public transport, facilities etc.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything was really smooth in terms of communication with UNIMI. Massimo Costa provided all the information needed, and if any help was required he would quickly respond.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance in terms of courses available, how to change courses and reassurance that courses could be changed during the stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing off campus since i didnt want to live in a shared room. Its fairly easy if you are going with friends in advance to find something together, but get it done as early as possible. The housing situation in Milan is ridiculous. I had to find something for my self, ended living in a hostel for the first week since there were issues with my prior agreement. After a week I found an expensive alternative through AirBNB.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its great if you can find something reasonable, but start searching really early, and preferably with others that are going abroad. Be careful of scammers though.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online registration, just find the class you want and thats that.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help available through instructions by mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont panic, you can change everything while you are there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most courses are fairly easy. The level is lower than UCPH, however some courses did require time and commitment. The level is higher than say the US or Canada, so dont expect it to be a breeze unless you take easy classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All classes were smaller, some were lectures, som were more like normal classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Risk Management
Business History
Causal Inference and policy evaluation
Game Theory
Corporate finance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Business History
Causal Inference and policy evaluation
Game Theory

Business History equates to økonomisk historie and is really chill. Game theory equates to micro iii and is also transferable. Causal can be transferred as Applied econometrics, and the prof. is really good. The course does require attendance and some work.

questions.answer: Really expensive housing, get it sorted early. everything else is fine.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Prices were as expected, on the higher end compared to the rest of Italy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some sports and random stuff. Social activities were through an erasmus program.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See if you can get a cheap train card for regional travel. Go see the rest of Italy, and during the warmer months, go to the lakes if you can.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Felt right at place.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You have to get used to the large amount of homeless. The inequality is vast, so that's a bit of a shock when you first arrive.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The joy of life, easy going culture, welcoming people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get the housing sorted first. Communicate with those that are going abroad with you. Relax, dont worry too much, everything will get sorted in the end.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take some easy courses so you can have some free time as well. youre not going there to study, youre going there to enjoy another city.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing a new culture and getting a break from the normal everyday life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Housing

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
